title: test_vectors.py short-addr derive + dad_hash tests fail at HEAD (crc32_init missing from short_addr_assignment.json)
description: Discovered during full python pytest run while validating worker6-xxpn on main 68c6e60d6f; verified pre-existing via clean HEAD worktree (identical failures with no local modifications). 7 deterministic failures: 6x test_short_addr_derive_vector (all params) + test_dad_hash_algorithm_resolution. Cause: python/tests/test_vectors.py line ~3953 asserts vector["crc32_init"] == "0x4348454e" but committed test/vectors/short_addr_assignment.json vectors lack the crc32_init key (KeyError). Both files unmodified in working tree; drift introduced by an earlier commit (last vector regen 0afb92c647, last test edit 70209a4a83/660b9bf3bf). Fix: either regenerate short_addr_assignment.json with crc32_init fields or update the test to match the committed schema - decide which side is normative, do not weaken the test.
notes: Uncommitted vector updates in test/vectors/dad_hash_clarification.json and test/vectors/short_addr_dad.json. Resolution: CRC32-IEEE (0xedb88320 reflected poly, init 0x4348454e) is authoritative per spec 02-physical-link.md 4.5. Also ccp-interference.json updated.
close_reason: 7 failures gone: pytest python/tests/test_vectors.py = 751 passed (baseline), 0 failed. Sides decided and documented: the VECTOR FILES were aligned to CRC32-IEEE (normative side = implementation + committed tests per resolved project-LICHEN-bo37: python short_addr.derive_short_addr uses binascii.crc32 init 0x4348454e; Rust lichen-core LICHEN_CRC32_INITIAL=0x4348_454e; both consumers assert crc32_init/crc32_ieee). The working tree already contained a partial regen of short_addr_dad.json (concurrent session) fixing the 6 derive failures - verified every value with an independent bitwise CRC-32/ISO-HDLC + FNV-1a32 oracle (self-checked against public check values 0xCBF43926 / 0xE40C292C / 0x29B1): ALL PASS. Completed the fix: (1) dad_hash_clarification.json resolution block was stale (authoritative_algorithm=fnv1a32) contradicting its own updated CRC32-authoritative description, the Python test (test_vectors.py:5085) and the Rust test (short_addr_vectors.rs:85) - set authoritative_algorithm=crc32_ieee + initial_value=0x4348454e (test-required keys) with polynomial + rationale note; (2) independent oracle caught 3 latent value defects in dad_hash_clarification.json: full_crc32 0x0000056e -> 0x5dd5056e, full_fnv 0x373e1bbd -> 0xc0e31bbd (both had stored the truncated low-16 zero-extended), seed-mixing crc32_result/fnv1a_result mixed_eui64 used a big-endian seed XOR label (0011223344556676 -> 0011223345556677; impls use seed.to_le_bytes() into eui64[4..8], confirmed in both Python and Rust) and fnv1a_result.derived_addr_would_be 58742 -> 3424 (old value matched no documented convention); (3) short_addr_dad.json derived_hex 0x56e -> 0x056e (4-digit pad consistency with siblings). Cross-impl validation: cargo test -p lichen-core --test short_addr_vectors = 5/5 passed (that test was also failing at HEAD against the committed fnv JSON). The stale spec fnv pseudocode is filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-sp7r.
